My dear [Christabel](/person/329)

I am very sorry this sad check has fallen on all the bright hopes.[^1] I remember [Mrs Keble](/person/795) saying, when my [brother](/person/1624) lost his [first](/person/1632), how often it happens that the first fruits of a family are thus consecrated and taken, and become in time a happy remembrance.

[May](/person/351) has been hoping that [Minny](/person/927)’s baby may come today on its [great grandfather](/person/344)’s birthday, I wonder if it will.

Poor [Katie Lloyd](/person/887) is at Ramsgate, very lame.[^2]

I have a nice set of Will stories, some very funny and some very melancholy.[^3]

Your affectionate
C.M.

Yonge


[^1]: CMY commiserates on the death of Thomas Drake Coleridge (18 Feb-2 July 1877), eldest son of Christabel Coleridge’s brother Ernest Hartley Coleridge (1846-1920).
[^2]: May was Mary Frances Keble Coleridge (1824-1898), daughter of Sir John Taylor Coleridge (9 July 1790-1876).

Her niece Mary (Mackarness) Coleridge, who was married to Bernard Coleridge, was expecting a baby, [Geoffrey Duke Coleridge](/person/338), 3rd Lord Coleridge (23 July 1877–1955).

Katie (Johns) Lloyd, was the former Gosling, who had married in 1873 the Rev.

John Henry Lloyd, curate of Wormleighton.
[^3]: The Christmas 1877 number of MP consisted of stories on the theme \'Will\'.
